reference.title: Troubleshooting
reference.shortdesc: Find the symptom in the table, then try each solution in order. If the problem continues, contact an authorized service center.

section.p: Before you inspect or service any part, complete through the step that relieves pressure.

row.entry: Problem
Possible cause
Solution
Motor does not start
GFCI device has tripped
Press RESET on the GFCI device. If it trips again, stop using the machine and contact service.
Circuit breaker has tripped
Reset the breaker. Make sure no other devices run on the same circuit.
Engine does not start
Fuel valve or engine switch is off
Turn the fuel valve and engine switch to ON.
Oil level is low
Add oil to the upper mark on the dipstick. The low-oil shutdown prevents starting until the level is correct.
Pressure is trapped in the pump
Squeeze the spray gun trigger while you pull the starter cord.
Low or pulsing pressure
Not enough water supply
Open the water supply fully. Use a hose no longer than 50 ft (15 m) and check it for kinks.
Air in the system
Stop the machine and purge air as described in .
Nozzle is worn or partly blocked
Clear the nozzle with the cleaning pin, or replace it.
Water leaks at a hose connection
Connection is loose or O-ring is damaged
Tighten the connection by hand. Replace the O-ring if the leak continues.
Water drips from under the pump
Thermal relief valve is releasing hot water
This is normal after a long pause in bypass mode. Squeeze the trigger more often, or stop the machine during long breaks.
Detergent does not flow
High-pressure nozzle is installed
Install the black 65° soap nozzle. Detergent flows only at low pressure.
